- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast gently to avoid undershoot.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a spike in sentiment, apply a 1–2 day lag correction to prevent overshoot.  
- In periods of high volatility (e.g., sentiment swings ±0.5+), reduce forecast variance by smoothing toward recent 7-day average.  
- If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast in early days of 30d horizon, apply a 3–5 day downward bias correction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2–0.5) and forecast is consistently above true outcome, apply mean reversion bias toward 14-day moving average.
